meta.title: Contivo — Marketing on autopilot
meta.description: Contivo turns your website into brand memory, competitive intelligence and a publishing autopilot: it writes, reviews and posts for you, on a schedule you set.

nav.siteOnlyNotice: This site is translated, but Contivo writes your content in English or Persian.

intake.label: Start with the only thing it needs
intake.errorEmpty: Type the address of the site you want read.
intake.errorInvalid: That does not look like a website address.
intake.hint: Next is a short sign-up. The address comes with you.

actOne.headline: Give it your website. <accent>Keep</accent> the rest of your day.
actOne.body: Contivo reads your site into a brand memory, maps the competitors you actually have, and works out which keywords they leave open. Only then does it write — and only what survives a quality gate built to reject it.

evidence.note: Measured on an example workspace built from a public website while writing this page, not on a customer's account.

reel.headline: The whole loop, in twenty-two seconds.
reel.body: How one URL becomes a brand memory, a market map, a refusal, and a week of posts that published themselves.
reel.videoAlt: Animated walkthrough of Contivo: a website address is read into a brand memory, competitors are plotted on a positioning chart, ideation stays locked until the intelligence exists, a draft passes the quality gate, and a week fills with scheduled posts.
reel.caption: An animated explainer, not a screen recording — the screenshots further down are the real product. No sound.
reel.reducedNote: Paused because your system asks for reduced motion.

intelligence.headline: Most tools start from a blank prompt. <accent>That</accent> is why they read like one.
intelligence.brandTitle: Your brand, read back to you
intelligence.brandBody: Paste a URL. Contivo pulls out the business summary, the value proposition, the audience it is actually written for and the tone it is written in — then lets you correct all of it. Every draft afterwards is built from this, not from your prompt.
intelligence.brandAlt: Contivo's Brand Memory screen showing an extracted business summary, value proposition, target audience persona and brand tone tags.
intelligence.marketTitle: The market, with you on it
intelligence.marketBody: It finds competitors at your scale, checks they exist, and lets you throw out the ones that are not really yours. What survives gets scored on positioning charts built for your market — and you are plotted among them, not described in a paragraph.
intelligence.marketAlt: Contivo's competitive landscape chart plotting the customer's brand among discovered competitors by audience size and product sophistication.

actTwo.headline: It will not write <accent>yet</accent>.
actTwo.body: Ideation is locked until the intelligence underneath it exists. You cannot talk your way past this, and neither can the model. It is the whole reason the output is worth reading.
actTwo.chainAlt: Contivo's setup chain for a real workspace: brand memory, the market map, competitor keywords and a publishing channel done; deciding what the brand stands for is the next step.
actTwo.chainCaption: The real chain, in the real product. Each step unlocks only when the one before it has run.
actTwo.checksTitle: Checks that cannot be argued with

checks.limits: Platform limits and the word range you set
checks.blocklist: Your never-write-about list, in the body and not just the title

judge.scores: Scores brand fit, factual safety and clarity out of ten
judge.strictest: Factual safety is the strictest threshold of the three
judge.vetoes: Vetoes invented statistics, named studies and client anecdotes
judge.held: Both providers down? The post is held. Never published unreviewed.

actThree.headline: Then it writes, and it <accent>posts</accent>.
actThree.body: You set a cadence, the channels, and the hours it is allowed to publish in. It keeps the coming week full, spreads posts across your window, avoids repeating itself, and retries when the queue runs low. Nobody approves anything unless you want to.
actThree.cadenceValue: 1–14 posts a week, kept full 7 days ahead
actThree.windowValue: The days and local hours you choose
actThree.steeringValue: A goal, themes to lean into, topics to never touch
actThree.postAlt: Contivo's pipeline for a real workspace: LinkedIn posts it wrote, two published and one drafted with its publish schedule, each showing its word target.
actThree.postCaption: The pipeline of a real workspace, captured for this page.

channels.headline: Social through OAuth. Your own site through one key.
channels.body: Connect your LinkedIn profile once and Contivo posts to it on your behalf. For your own website — any stack, any host — you get an API key and your site reads its posts. Nothing is ever pushed into your codebase, and no plugin is installed. X is not switched on yet, and Instagram, Facebook and TikTok each need their platform's app review first.
channels.connectBody: One OAuth pass for LinkedIn, or one key for your site.
channels.scheduleBody: Contivo picks slots inside the window you allowed.
channels.publishBody: A scheduler fires every minute and posts what is due.
channels.recordBody: Every run is logged, step by step, including what it rejected.

close.headline: Paste a URL and go back to <accent>work</accent>.
close.body: Sign up, hand it your address, and it reads your site into a brand memory and a competitive map. From there the queue fills itself, and the only thing it will not do is publish something it could not stand behind.

hero.headline: Your LinkedIn and your blog, <accent>kept busy</accent> every week.
hero.body: Give Contivo your website. It learns what you sell and who you compete with, then writes posts for your LinkedIn and articles for your own site, and publishes them on the days you choose. Each one is checked before it goes out.
hero.shotAlt: The pipeline of a real Contivo workspace: posts published to LinkedIn and one draft waiting for its slot.
hero.shotCaption: A real workspace, captured from the app: posts published to LinkedIn, one draft scheduled.

posts.title: 1 to 14 posts a week
posts.body: You choose how many. It keeps the next seven days planned.

channels.title: Your LinkedIn and your own site
channels.body: Posts on your personal LinkedIn profile, articles on your website. X, Telegram, WordPress and Threads are on the way.

time.title: On the days and hours you pick
time.body: In your time zone, spread out so two posts on the same idea never land back to back.

s1.title: It reads your site
s1.body: What you do, what you promise, who it's for and how you sound, written back for you to correct.
s1.alt: Brand memory in a real workspace: business summary, value proposition, audience and tone.

s2.title: It researches your market
s2.body: Competitors your size, checked to exist and plotted against you, with the gaps they leave open.
s2.alt: A positioning chart in a real workspace, with the brand plotted among its competitors.

s3.title: It writes and publishes
s3.body: Drafts in your voice, each tied to a storyline and checked, then posted to LinkedIn and your site on schedule.
s3.alt: The pipeline of a real workspace, with posts published to LinkedIn.

notAi.title: Why it won't read like everyone else's AI
notAi.body: Most tools start writing from a blank prompt. Contivo won't produce a single idea until it has your brand memory and your competitor research, and every draft then goes through a gate built to reject it.
notAi.compareLink: How it compares with other tools

pricing.title: What it costs
pricing.body: New accounts are free during early access. Once billing starts:

publish.a: By default, yes: posts that pass the quality gate go out on schedule. Turn on approval and every draft waits for you instead.

channels.a: Your personal LinkedIn profile, and your own website through a read-only API that a developer connects once. Company pages, X, Telegram, WordPress and Threads are not live yet.

languages.q: Which languages does it write in?
languages.a: English and Persian. This site is in more languages than that, but the content Contivo writes is in one of those two.

cost.a: Nothing for new accounts during early access. After that, from $55 a month.

need.q: What do I need to start?
need.a: A website. To post on LinkedIn, your LinkedIn account; to publish on your site, a developer for one short setup.

footer.blurb: Reads your website into brand memory and a competitive map, then writes, reviews and publishes on a schedule you set.
footer.provenance: Built and run first on its own sites. 23 early-access users have paid for it since; none is named here without their say-so.
